title: fix(test-config): state a true reason in the dist-pins guard, and pin it
body:
Fixes #8274

The `DIST_PINS_ENABLED` guard in `vitest.config.mts` refused `vitest --project dist` with a justification that was false about vitest. The guard stays; only its reason changes, plus a pin so the reason cannot rot again.

## The probe, re-derived on this branch

Exit code captured by redirect before any pipe. vitest `4.1.10 linux-x64 node-v22.22.2`.

```
$ pnpm exec vitest run --project @object-ui/does-not-exist
Error: No projects matched the filter "@object-ui/does-not-exist".
exit 1
```

The card's premise holds. An unresolvable `--project` is loud, not green.

**And measured on the real name**, by ablating the guard itself (`if (false && DIST_PROJECT_NAMED ...)`), so the reading is about `dist` rather than a proxy — mutation proven on disk (blob `77a40ce4` to `4d791046`), restore proven byte-identical back to `77a40ce4` with `git diff HEAD` empty:

```
$ pnpm exec vitest run --project dist        # guard ablated, OBJECTUI_DIST_PINS unset
Error: No projects matched the filter "dist".
exit 1
```

So the un-opted run has never been a false green on vitest 4. What it *is* — and this is the guard's real justification — is a dead end: that refusal names neither `OBJECTUI_DIST_PINS` nor `pnpm test:dist`, so it stops the reader without telling them there is a remedy.

## The message, before and after

Before:

```
'vitest --project dist was requested, but OBJECTUI_DIST_PINS is not "1", so the',
'`dist` project is NOT declared and this run would collect ZERO files and exit GREEN.',
```

After:

```
'vitest --project dist was requested, but OBJECTUI_DIST_PINS is not "1", so the',
'`dist` project is NOT declared. Left to vitest, this run ends in its generic',
'refusal - `No projects matched the filter "dist"`, exit 1 - which tells you the',
'filter matched nothing but not that the project is env-gated, and names neither',
'OBJECTUI_DIST_PINS nor the task that sets it. Hence this message.',
```

The remaining five lines of the message (what the `dist` project holds, `pnpm test:dist`, the pointers) are unchanged — that half was always true and is the half worth keeping. The comment block above the guard carried the same false premise and is rewritten with it; it now quotes the retracted sentence deliberately, as the record of what was corrected.

## Four axes — why this wording

- **实际业务需求.** Measured, not hypothetical: the filing seat reached for this sentence while deciding whether a `--project`-based package script needed an empty-collection guard, could not trust it, and had to go measure vitest. The wording is chosen to answer the question that reader actually had — *what happens if I ignore this and run it anyway* — because that is the question a refusal message is read for.
- **项目长远合理性.** Contract-first, applied to prose: the guard's premise is a claim about a dependency's behaviour, so it is stated as what that dependency does, at the granularity someone can check. No workaround, no hedge, no deletion of a guard whose value was never in the false sentence.
- **防 AI 写代码犯错.** The old sentence taught a specific wrong lesson — "vitest silently greens on a bad `--project` name" — which generalises to "every `--project` call site needs a name-validity guard". It does not and they do not; the genuinely silent case is a project that *resolves* and then globs zero files, a different mechanism with a different remedy (`--no-passWithNoTests`, as objectui#8240 uses). Stating the true behaviour keeps that distinction intact instead of blurring two failure modes into one.
- **创业阶段不扩散需求.** No new surface, no new option, no staged deprecation: five lines of message text and one test file. The guard's behaviour is byte-for-byte what it was.

## Sweep

Grepped the tree for the same reasoning — `exit GREEN` / `exits green` / `collect ZERO files` / `zero files` / `matched no project` / `passWithNoTests` across `*.ts`, `*.tsx`, `*.mts`, `*.mjs`, `*.js`, `*.md`, `*.json`, `*.yml`.

- **Sites found asserting vitest's behaviour on an unresolvable `--project`: 2.** `vitest.config.mts` (the throw and its comment — corrected here) and `scripts/__tests__/app-test-entry-8240.test.ts`.
- **Corrected: 1** (`vitest.config.mts`, both the throw text and the comment).
- **Left alone: 1.** `app-test-entry-8240.test.ts` states the opposite and states it correctly: *"a project name that resolves to nothing is loud: vitest throws `No projects matched the filter "..."` (measured: exit 1); but a project that resolves and then globs zero files is SILENT"*. My probe corroborates it verbatim.

Everything else the grep turned up (`scripts/vitest-invocation-guard.mjs`, `package-scripts-vitest-projects.test.ts`, the various "a gate that scanned zero files is not a gate" comments) is about path filters or empty collections, not about project resolution. Nothing there is proven false by this probe, so nothing there is touched.

## Pin decision — the strong form, because it turned out to be cheap

`scripts/__tests__/dist-pins-guard-message-8274.test.ts`, five cases, **2.03s** for the whole file.

The trade as stated in the brief: a grep pin is weak, a spawn pin is strong but costs a vitest spawn. I priced the spawn before choosing — **1675ms**, because the run dies during project resolution and never builds a test graph. That price makes the argument one-sided, so the pin measures the fact:

- two spawns of a real vitest with an undeclared project name, asserting the loud non-zero exit **and** that vitest's own message mentions neither `OBJECTUI_DIST_PINS` nor `test:dist` (both halves of the justification the guard now states);
- one spawn of `--project dist` with the env var unset, asserting the guard fires and the reader gets *this* message;
- and the cheap static half — the thrown text must not regress to a silent-green claim.

A grep-only pin would have stayed green in the one direction that matters: vitest changing to swallow the bad filter and exit 0. It also invites the repair of editing the sentence until the grep passes. The spawn cannot be satisfied that way.

Both legs reverse-verified from a committed state, each with a `trap`-guarded restore and byte-identical restoration proven by blob hash:

| mutation | expected | observed |
|---|---|---|
| reinstate the false sentence in the throw | static case reds | `× does not claim the un-opted run exits green or collects zero files` — 1 failed, 4 passed |
| ablate the guard (`if (false && ...)`) | the guard-fires case reds | `× fires for --project dist without the env var, and reaches the reader first` — 1 failed, 4 passed |

One assertion was deliberately dropped during that work and the reason is recorded in the test: on a config-load failure vitest echoes the config **source** back, and that source now quotes `No projects matched the filter` verbatim, so asserting its absence would fail for a reason unrelated to project resolution.

## Gates — each by redirect, exit code captured before any pipe

| gate | exit |
|---|---|
| `pnpm exec vitest run scripts/__tests__/dist-pins-guard-message-8274.test.ts` | **0** (5 passed, 2.03s) |
| `pnpm exec vitest run scripts/__tests__/` | **0** (121 files, 3580 tests) — see note below |
| `pnpm lint:root` | **0** (0 errors; the 32 warnings are pre-existing, none in the changed files) |
| `pnpm type-check:scripts` | **0** |
| `pnpm check:control-bytes` | **0** (6649 tracked text files) |
| `pnpm check:comment-mask-corpus` | **0** (within the residue objectui#7882 holds open) |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` | **0** — "no changeset is owed": 2 files changed, 0 of them published source, 0 a manifest whose published contract moved |
| `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` on both changed paths | **0** — NOT GOVERNED, 2 paths against 5 governed surfaces |

Guard behaviour, directly:

| invocation | result |
|---|---|
| `pnpm exec vitest run --project dist`, `OBJECTUI_DIST_PINS` unset | throws with the new message, exit 1 |
| `OBJECTUI_DIST_PINS=1 pnpm exec vitest list --project dist` | guard silent, `dist` project resolves and lists its pins, exit 0 |

`pnpm check:lint-rule-coverage` was not run — the known defect objectui#8369.

**One note on the suite run, in the interest of not overclaiming.** `scripts/__tests__/` was run twice. The first (88.04s) was green. The second, during heavy container contention (191.11s), had one failure: `check-unused-dependencies.test.ts` → *"is green: every gated declaration has a consumer"*, `Test timed out in 15000ms` at 16037ms. Re-run in isolation it is green (37 passed, exit 0), and it is untouched by this diff — it scans `package.json` dependency declarations. It is a load-sensitive flake, filed separately as #8380 rather than shrugged at.

## Out of scope, filed

- #8380 — `check-unused-dependencies.test.ts`'s whole-repo scan inherits the 15s default `testTimeout` and flakes under container load. Unassigned, unlabelled, left for triage.
